hints: An Euler path uses every directed edge exactly once, starting at 1 and ending at n.
Check degree conditions: start has one extra outgoing edge, end one extra incoming, and all others balance.
Run Hierholzer from 1 and verify every edge was used and the route ends at n.
analogy: The route must balance every intermediate city and use every teleport exactly once.
example: For two edges 1->2 and 2->3, route 1,2,3 starts at 1 and ends at 3 using both.
algorithm: Check in-degree/out-degree conditions, then run iterative Hierholzer from 1; reverse the circuit and require m+1 vertices with endpoints 1,n.
correctness: The degree conditions are necessary for an Euler trail, and Hierholzer constructs one when all edges are reachable in the required trail; edge-count verification rejects disconnected leftovers.
